question: Why must food be digested before your body can absorb it?

options.A: Digestion adds essential vitamins that trigger active transport
options.B: The stomach cannot hold food unless it is first broken down
options.C: Unbroken food particles will immediately cause an immune reaction
options.D: Complex molecules are too large to cross the intestinal mucosal lining

explanation: Think of it like trying to pass a big couch through a tiny doorway—large food molecules simply cannot fit across the intestinal wall until they are chopped down into smaller pieces!

question: Your catheterized patient has had no urine output for two hours and feels lower belly discomfort. What do you check first?

options.A: Check the tubing for kinks, twists, or compression under the patient
options.B: Call the doctor to report acute kidney failure
options.C: Remove the catheter immediately and insert a new one
options.D: Inject sterile water into the balloon to secure it further

explanation: Always look for the simple fix first! A twisted or flattened tube is usually the culprit when urine suddenly stops flowing.

question: What should you do immediately if a patient says a warm compress feels like it is burning their skin?

options.A: Press the compress down harder to ensure even contact
options.B: Administer an oral pain medication and leave the compress on
options.C: Remove the compress immediately and inspect the skin
options.D: Wait five minutes to see if the skin adjusts to the heat

explanation: If a patient says it burns, take it off right away and check the skin. Never ignore a burn complaint!

question: Why is suddenly stopping long-term steroid therapy so dangerous (leading to an addisonian crisis)?

options.A: The kidneys start excreting all remaining sodium and water within minutes
options.B: The sudden lack of steroids causes a massive uncontrolled surge of white blood cells
options.C: The adrenal glands have atrophied and cannot immediately produce natural cortisol
options.D: The liver immediately stops filtering toxins out of the circulating bloodstream

explanation: Since the adrenal glands were resting while taking synthetic pills, they can't instantly wake up and make natural cortisol when you stop abruptly. This causes a dangerous drop in blood pressure and shock.

question: If you are posted as a nurse to a new displacement camp, what major environmental challenge should you expect?

options.A: Immediate surplus of specialized surgical equipment
options.B: Excessive availability of modern private housing
options.C: Complete absence of any communicable diseases
options.D: Overcrowding and limited access to clean water

explanation: New camps often spring up overnight, leading to heavy crowding and tough living conditions. As nurses, anticipating clean water shortages helps us prevent disease outbreaks!

question: Which mask is most important when doing a procedure that generates aerosols on a COVID-19 patient?

options.A: A standard cloth face covering
options.B: A disposable paper surgical mask
options.C: A simple clear plastic face shield alone
options.D: An N95 or higher respirator mask

explanation: That's correct! Procedures that create tiny floating mists require the tight seal and special filtration of an N95 respirator to keep you safe.

question: Why must nurses treat used clinical items as places where germs actively grow?

options.A: Because hospital trash is legally classified as hazardous material automatically
options.B: Because cleaning staff refuse to handle items unless they are labeled alive
options.C: Because used items contain moisture and nutrients that help microbes multiply
options.D: Because all discarded items will immediately begin to emit toxic gases

explanation: Spot on! Things like used dressings and body fluids provide a warm, wet home full of nutrients. Germs love this and will multiply rapidly if we don't contain them properly.

question: A patient asks what happens to sperm immediately after they are created in the seminiferous tubules. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: They travel to the epididymis to mature.
options.B: They enter the prostate gland for activation.
options.C: They mix with urine in the urinary bladder.
options.D: They travel directly out through the penile skin.

explanation: After leaving the seminiferous tubules, sperm move into the duct system and head directly into the epididymis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a common home hazard that causes older adults to fall?

options.A: Brightly lit hallway floors
options.B: Low pile carpeting securely glued to the floor
options.C: Loose scatter rugs and cluttered pathways
options.D: Sturdy grab bars installed near the toilet

explanation: Correct! Loose rugs and messy walkways are classic traps that easily trip up older people. Good thing to watch out for in clinical practice!

question: What happens to a patient's red blood cells if they are given a severely hypotonic intravenous solution?

options.A: They remain completely unchanged
options.B: They immediately multiply rapidly
options.C: They swell and may burst
options.D: They shrink and shrivel up

explanation: In a hypotonic solution, water rushes into the cells because the surrounding fluid has a lower solute concentration, causing the cells to swell and potentially rupture (lysis). [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which key parts of the body work together to control the normal female monthly cycle?

options.A: Thyroid, adrenal glands, and pancreas
options.B: Brain and outer blood vessels
options.C: Hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and ovaries
options.D: Heart and lungs

explanation: You've got this! The hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and ovaries form the main hormonal team (the HPO axis) that drives the female reproductive cycle.

question: Why are palliative patients at such high risk for developing pressure injuries?

options.A: Poor mobility, reduced tissue perfusion, and loss of subcutaneous fat
options.B: They sweat excessively due to high room temperatures
options.C: They consume too many high-fat foods in their daily diet
options.D: Skin cells multiply at a dangerously fast rate near the end of life

explanation: Decreased blood flow, immobility, and wasting tissues make the skin fragile and vulnerable to breakdown. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h7)

question: Which fluid fills the large cavity behind the lens to keep the retina in place?

options.A: Aqueous humor
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: Synovial fluid
options.D: Vitreous humor

explanation: Vitreous humor is a thick gel that fills the posterior segment and keeps the eyeball from collapsing. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h3)

question: Storing kerosene inside an empty soft drink bottle is an example of which type of risk factor at home?

options.A: Chronic medical illness
options.B: Hereditary predisposition
options.C: Environmental hazard
options.D: Psychological disorder

explanation: Putting dangerous liquids in drink bottles creates an unsafe home environment that easily leads to accidental poisoning or burns.

question: A patient doing a 24-hour urine collection tells you they accidentally flushed one sample halfway through the day. What should you do?

options.A: Discard the current collection and restart the entire 24-hour process
options.B: Estimate the missed amount and add extra water to make up the volume
options.C: Extend the collection period by twelve hours to make up for the loss
options.D: Send the incomplete jug to the lab with a note explaining the lost sample

explanation: Ah, frustration! But a 24-hour test has to be complete. Missing even one bathroom trip means the numbers won't be accurate, so it's best to start fresh another day.

question: What is the main dietary focus when caring for a patient with high blood pressure (hypertension)?

options.A: Sodium restriction
options.B: Zero fluid consumption
options.C: High protein loading
options.D: Unlimited sugar intake

explanation: You know this! Cutting down on salt (sodium) helps reduce fluid retention and lowers pressure inside the blood vessels.

question: What does a decline in 'executive function' look like for a patient?

options.A: Trouble with planning, organizing, and solving problems
options.B: Constant involuntary shaking of the hands
options.C: A complete inability to feel physical pain
options.D: Sudden loss of the ability to swallow food

explanation: Executive functions are like the brain's manager—they help us plan our day, organize tasks, and solve everyday problems.

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a school health programme?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community health workers
options.B: To penalize teachers whose classes have poor attendance records
options.C: To measure success, identify gaps, and improve service delivery
options.D: To calculate the exact financial profits of the school canteen

explanation: Correct! Checking in on the programme helps us see what is working well and fix areas that need more attention.

question: What was the main problem with most ancient birth control methods?

options.A: They were too expensive for ordinary citizens to purchase
options.B: They were frequently toxic, unreliable, or completely ineffective
options.C: They required advanced surgical equipment available only to royalty
options.D: They relied on electronic monitoring of the menstrual cycle

explanation: Ancient remedies relied a lot on guesswork and folk traditions, which often meant they didn't work well and could even be unsafe.

question: Why are teenagers often more prone to screen addiction than older adults?

options.A: Their prefrontal cortex is still maturing, making impulse control difficult
options.B: They have more financial resources to purchase high-end gadgets
options.C: They spend less time sleeping than adults do on average
options.D: Their eyes are more sensitive to the blue light emitted by screens

explanation: Think about brain development! The part of the brain that helps with self-control and good judgment is still growing in teens, making it harder to put the phone down.

question: A nurse is gently pressing on a patient's abdomen to check for tenderness and masses. Which physical examination technique is the nurse using?

options.A: Auscultation
options.B: Palpation
options.C: Inspection
options.D: Percussion

explanation: Palpation involves using the hands and fingers to feel parts of the body for tenderness, lumps, or abnormal size. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h2)

question: Which of these nursing actions goes completely against the ethical rules of HCT?

options.A: Keeping a client's positive test result private from their employer
options.B: Providing pre-test counselling before drawing blood for screening
options.C: Performing an HIV test on a competent adult without their consent
options.D: Offering routine testing to all pregnant women attending antenatal care

explanation: Great job! Testing someone without their knowledge or clear agreement is a major breach of patient rights and medical ethics.

question: Why is involving local community members in school health campaigns advantageous?

options.A: They possess formal degrees in advanced medical epidemiology
options.B: They receive massive salaries from international health organizations
options.C: They have legal authority to penalize parents who refuse treatment
options.D: They understand local cultural nuances and speak the local language

explanation: Local members communicate health messages in ways that resonate deeply with the community's beliefs and language. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why does empowering women often lead to smaller, more planned families?

options.A: Employers legally restrict female workers from starting families
options.B: Women lose their biological capacity to conceive after higher education
options.C: Women gain greater decision-making power over their reproductive health
options.D: Government laws force educated women to have fewer children

explanation: Spot on! When women are empowered, they have a stronger voice in deciding family size and birth spacing.

question: What usually triggers the body to develop secondary polycythaemia?

options.A: An autoimmune attack on bone marrow
options.B: An inherited defect in the platelets
options.C: Sudden heavy blood loss from injury
options.D: Chronic low oxygen levels in tissues

explanation: Spot on! When body tissues are short on oxygen over time, the body panics and pumps out more red blood cells to help.

question: What is the best nursing action when preparing a newly diagnosed patient for lifelong HIV treatment?

options.A: Providing clear, simple education on drug action, side effects, and adherence
options.B: Telling the patient to hide all pill bottles away from family members
options.C: Insisting that the patient stop working to focus entirely on health
options.D: Withholding information about side effects so the patient does not worry

explanation: You nailed it! Empowering patients with simple, honest education sets them up to manage their health with confidence.

question: According to the IASC intervention pyramid, which tier represents specialized mental health care given by professionals?

options.A: Tier 4
options.B: Tier 1
options.C: Tier 2
options.D: Tier 3

explanation: Tier 4 sits right at the top of the IASC pyramid. It's where specialists step in with clinical treatments for patients who need deeper care.

question: Why is good nutrition during early childhood so important?

options.A: Deficits during this window can cause permanent stunting and brain damage
options.B: Young children have fully developed organs that process food slowly
options.C: It prevents the child from ever catching infections later in life
options.D: Children naturally require fewer nutrients than adults do

explanation: Think of early childhood as a critical construction phase. Missing key nutrients here can unfortunately lead to lasting effects on growth and brain development.

question: Which of these would stop you from using a tympanic thermometer safely?

options.A: A buildup of earwax blocking the ear canal
options.B: The patient just drank some water
options.C: A history of mild seasonal allergies
options.D: Mild dehydration without a fever

explanation: Excess wax blocks the path to the eardrum, meaning the sensor won't catch the right heat radiation.

question: What is the classic sign that patients usually report when they have a bone tumor?

options.A: Itchy skin rashes directly over the affected joint
options.B: Sudden numbness and tingling in the toes of both feet
options.C: Persistent, worsening bone pain that is often present at night
options.D: Sharp shooting pain that only happens during heavy physical exercise

explanation: Unlike normal muscle aches, bone tumor pain is relentless, gets worse over time, and loves to wake patients up at night.

question: Why should a nurse assess a patient's swallowing ability before giving oral pills?

options.A: To prevent choking and potential aspiration into the lungs
options.B: To see if the patient has any food allergies
options.C: To check how fast the liver will metabolize the drug
options.D: To determine if the patient prefers liquid or solid medicines

explanation: Swallowing difficulties place patients at high risk of aspirating foreign objects or liquids into the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which enzyme in the liver changes unconjugated bilirubin into a water-soluble form?

options.A: Lactase dehydrogenase
options.B: Amylase and lipase
options.C: Glucuronyl transferase
options.D: Alkaline phosphatase

explanation: Glucuronyl transferase is the key liver enzyme responsible for conjugating bilirubin so the body can excrete it safely. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h2)

question: What is another common name for the normal bacteria and microbes living on and inside the human body?

options.A: Human microbiota
options.B: Somatic organisms
options.C: Pathogenic colonies
options.D: Acellular particles

explanation: You've got this! 'Human microbiota' is just the scientific term for the friendly community of microbes that call our bodies home. Every healthy person has them!

question: Where must a urinary catheter collection bag be positioned at all times to prevent backflow?

options.A: Below the level of the bladder
options.B: Resting on the floor of the room
options.C: Attached to the patient's pillow
options.D: Level with the patient's hip

explanation: Gravity keeps urine flowing downward away from the bladder, preventing contaminated urine from flowing back up into the tubing. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: What do agonal gasps mean when you are checking an unresponsive patient?

options.A: The patient is recovering normal respiratory function
options.B: The airway is completely blocked by a foreign object
options.C: The patient is having a mild asthma attack
options.D: The patient is experiencing cardiac arrest and needs immediate CPR

explanation: Agonal gasps look like struggling breaths, but they are actually just body reflexes. They tell you the heart has stopped and it's time to start compressions!

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: To eliminate all potential discomforts of pregnancy
options.B: To prevent the fetus from moving into a breech position
options.C: To detect silent conditions like high blood pressure early
options.D: To guarantee a normal vaginal delivery date

explanation: You got it! Some dangerous issues like high blood pressure don't show early signs, which is why regular clinic checks are so important.

question: Why is collaboration with traditional birth attendants and local volunteers important for a PHC nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need for government-supplied medications
options.B: It ensures that traditional workers stop practicing completely
options.C: It fosters teamwork and bridges traditional practices with formal health services
options.D: It allows the nurse to transfer all clinical responsibilities to volunteers

explanation: Collaborating with local groups helps guide traditional practices safely and encourages mothers to seek formal care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which assessment is essential when checking a newborn's skull after a difficult birth with heavy moulding?

options.A: Checking deep tendon reflexes in the lower extremities only
options.B: Performing a lumbar puncture immediately on all babies
options.C: Measuring head circumference and assessing fontanelle texture
options.D: Aspirating fluid from the suture lines with a small needle

explanation: Correct! Checking the head size and feeling whether the fontanelles are soft, flat, or bulging helps you catch any hidden swelling early.

question: A postpartum mother has a tender, firm lump in one breast with mild redness, but no fever. What should the nurse suggest?

options.A: Encourage warm compresses, breast massage, and frequent nursing on the affected side.
options.B: Advise immediate cessation of breastfeeding and application of tight chest binders.
options.C: Administer a dose of oxytocin nasal spray to induce systemic breast involution.
options.D: Refer her urgently for a surgical biopsy to rule out malignancy.

explanation: This sounds like a blocked milk duct. Warmth, gentle massage, and keeping the baby feeding on that side will help clear the blockage right up.

question: What type of waste belongs inside a puncture-resistant safety box?

options.A: Expired food scraps
options.B: Contaminated paperwork
options.C: Empty water bottles
options.D: Sharps and needles

explanation: Safety boxes are specially designed to safely contain sharp objects like needles and blades without letting them pierce through. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which protective gear is a must-have when working near an active X-ray machine?

options.A: Thick rubber industrial gloves
options.B: Lead apron and thyroid collar
options.C: N95 respiratory face mask
options.D: Waterproof plastic shoe covers

explanation: Lead aprons and thyroid shields act like a block, stopping harmful radiation from reaching your sensitive organs and tissues.

question: Why do midwives and nurses perform Leopold's maneuvers when a mother is admitted?

options.A: To assess fetal lie, presentation, and position
options.B: To check for signs of a postpartum infection
options.C: To measure cervical dilation in centimeters
options.D: To determine the exact gestational age in weeks

explanation: You're doing great! Leopold's maneuvers are simply systematic hand movements on the tummy to figure out how the baby is lying before doing an internal check.

question: What is the primary purpose of administering furosemide to a patient with acute renal failure and fluid overload?

options.A: To permanently repair damaged glomeruli in the nephrons
options.B: To dissolve large kidney stones blocking the ureters
options.C: To lower dangerous levels of blood glucose in the body
options.D: To stimulate urine output and reduce excess body fluid

explanation: Loop diuretics like furosemide help the kidneys excrete excess water and sodium when the patient is fluid overloaded. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do if a patient reacts badly to an IV medication?

options.A: Give an oral allergy tablet
options.B: Write down the exact time in the chart
options.C: Leave the room to find the doctor
options.D: Stop the medication infusion right away

explanation: Safety first! Stopping the drug immediately keeps any more of the bad stuff from entering the patient's body.

question: What physical examination technique involves using a stethoscope to listen to internal body sounds?

options.A: Palpation
options.B: Inspection
options.C: Percussion
options.D: Auscultation

explanation: Auscultation is the act of listening to sounds within the body, such as the heart and lungs, using a stethoscope. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the time frame for defining puerperal sepsis following childbirth?

options.A: Strictly during the active stage of labor
options.B: Within the first 42 days postpartum
options.C: Between 6 weeks and 3 months postpartum
options.D: Only during the first 24 hours postpartum

explanation: Puerperal sepsis is officially defined as an infection of the genital tract occurring anytime from the onset of membrane rupture or labor up to 42 days following delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h1)

question: What defines a faith-based organization in the health sector?

options.A: It is owned and operated by religious institutions
options.B: It functions exclusively as a commercial pharmacy chain
options.C: It receives all its funding directly from the federal tax board
options.D: It only treats patients who share a specific political view

explanation: Exactly! Faith-based clinics and hospitals are run by religious bodies and provide vital care right in our local communities.

question: Which simple tip helps your body absorb oral albendazole much better?

options.A: Ingesting the medication with a fatty meal
options.B: Crushing the tablet and dissolving it in cold water
options.C: Avoiding all fluids for two hours after dosing
options.D: Taking the pill on an empty stomach with vinegar

explanation: That's correct! Taking albendazole with a bit of fat helps your body absorb it much more effectively.

question: How does stomach acid help protect you from getting sick?

options.A: By coating the intestinal lining with a thick mucus
options.B: By destroying ingested bacteria and other microorganisms
options.C: By producing specific antibodies against food antigens
options.D: By stimulating the production of white blood cells

explanation: Exactly! The strong acid in your stomach acts like a harsh chemical bath that kills most of the germs you accidentally swallow with your food or water.

question: You notice continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber of a chest tube system. What does this usually mean?

options.A: An expected amount of residual blood loss
options.B: An air leak somewhere in the tubing or insertion site
options.C: Blockage of the chest tube drainage lumen
options.D: Normal lung re-expansion and healing

explanation: While tiny occasional bubbles can be normal, continuous bubbling is like a leaky bicycle tire telling us air is getting in where it shouldn't. Excellent clinical observation!

question: What is a key part of preparing ahead of time for a home birth?

options.A: Educating the family on recognizing pregnancy danger signs
options.B: Booking a hospital bed just in case labor fails to start
options.C: Purchasing expensive medical monitors for the bedroom
options.D: Administering routine general anesthesia at 36 weeks

explanation: Knowledge is power! Teaching the family signs like heavy bleeding or severe headaches helps them call for help early if something goes wrong.

question: What is a vital safety step when nursing a patient with Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: Setting up fall precautions because of poor coordination
options.B: Encouraging heavy gym workouts to build leg strength
options.C: Restricting all fluids to stop brain swelling
options.D: Keeping the room pitch black all day

explanation: Spot on! Because these patients struggle with balance (ataxia), keeping them safe from nasty falls is a top nursing priority.

question: What is a very common physical change patients notice after they start eating a healthier diet?

options.A: Immediate growth in height as an adult
options.B: Permanent loss of the need for sleep
options.C: Reduced fatigue and higher energy levels
options.D: Complete immunity to all viral infections

explanation: You got it! Giving the body proper fuel works wonders—patients are often amazed at how much lighter and more energetic they feel.

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in maternal health programs?

options.A: To punish nurses who make mistakes during night shifts
options.B: To track progress, spot system weaknesses, and guide proper resource use
options.C: To reduce the number of women attending antenatal care
options.D: To increase the cost of medications in government clinics

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation provide data that shows what is working and where urgent improvements are needed in the healthcare system. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h8)

question: Which type of germ is usually behind a sudden outbreak of waterborne stomach illness?

options.A: Degenerative nerve proteins
options.B: Bacterial and viral agents
options.C: Autoimmune antibodies
options.D: Hereditary genetic mutations

explanation: When drinking water gets contaminated, harmful bacteria and viruses easily find their way in and cause stomach upsets.

question: Why should a nurse check local market days and religious schedules before setting a date for a community health talk?

options.A: To comply with international trade and economic regulations
options.B: To avoid scheduling conflicts that would prevent people from attending
options.C: To make sure the weather is always cool and rainy
options.D: To ensure the nurse can buy fresh food items after the meeting

explanation: You nailed it! Checking local routines ensures you pick a time when people are actually free to show up and learn.

question: What does the potency of a medication tell us?

options.A: The percentage of medicine lost in the stomach
options.B: The speed at which the liver breaks down the pill
options.C: The total maximum effect the drug can achieve
options.D: The amount of drug needed to produce a specific effect

explanation: Potency is all about dosage size. A highly potent drug packs a big punch even in a tiny dose!

question: What food safety rule is most important for a patient with a severely weakened immune system?

options.A: Eat only thoroughly cooked foods and avoid raw fruits or unpasteurized dairy
options.B: Consume raw salads daily to increase natural vitamin and fiber intake
options.C: Eat street foods as long as they are served at room temperature
options.D: Drink fresh unpasteurized milk to boost beneficial gut bacteria

explanation: You got it! Raw foods and unpasteurized dairy can hide sneaky bacteria and parasites that a healthy body handles easily, but can overwhelm a weak immune system.

question: Why is male involvement important in family planning decisions?

options.A: It reduces the cost of buying medications
options.B: It gives men total control over family size
options.C: It removes the need for female contraceptive use
options.D: It ensures joint agreement and supports birth spacing

explanation: Family planning works best when both partners discuss and agree on methods that protect the health of the mother. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h4)

question: How does teamwork between nurses, doctors, and pharmacists improve the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: By removing the need for any internal hospital quality audits
options.B: By allowing nurses to take over surgical operations from physicians
options.C: By shifting all financial responsibilities entirely onto patients
options.D: By combining different professional skills to prevent drug errors and waste

explanation: Spot on! When healthcare professionals team up, they catch mistakes early and keep patients safe.

question: Why is it so important to keep pauses in chest compressions as short as possible when using an AED?

options.A: Pauses reduce blood flow to the heart and brain, lowering survival rates.
options.B: Pauses allow the patient's body temperature to drop too quickly.
options.C: Pauses confuse the AED computer and prevent rhythm analysis.
options.D: Pauses cause the AED battery to drain faster during the rescue.

explanation: Every second you stop pumping, blood stops flowing to the brain. Keeping compressions continuous gives the patient the best fighting chance.

question: Why is keeping a hospital ward calm and clean during mealtime so important?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to clean bedsheets
options.B: It speeds up the digestion rate in the stomach
options.C: It stops patients from talking to one another
options.D: It encourages better appetite and food consumption

explanation: Spot on! A peaceful, clean, and pleasant dining vibe lowers stress and makes patients actually want to eat their meals.

question: How does carrying extra body weight affect weight-bearing joints like the knees?

options.A: By drying out the synovial fluid completely
options.B: By stopping blood flow to the bone marrow
options.C: By increasing chemical toxins in the blood
options.D: By placing continuous mechanical stress on weight-bearing joints

explanation: Well done! Extra weight means extra physical pressure on joints like your knees and hips with every single step you take.

question: In which part of the fallopian tube does fertilization of the ovum normally take place?

options.A: The ampulla
options.B: The fimbriae
options.C: The interstitial segment
options.D: The isthmus

explanation: The wider ampulla section provides the ideal space and environment for the sperm to meet and fertilize the released egg. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h1)

question: What is the recommended minimum time for brushing teeth properly?

options.A: Two full minutes
options.B: Five exact minutes
options.C: Thirty total seconds
options.D: Ten brief seconds

explanation: Brushing for at least two minutes gives you enough time to reach all tooth surfaces and get rid of stubborn plaque.

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a patient first believe before changing a health habit?

options.A: They are at personal risk of a serious health problem
options.B: Every member of their village has already changed
options.C: They can afford expensive private hospital care
options.D: The government will pay for all their medical bills

explanation: People rarely change unless they feel vulnerable. The model shows that recognizing personal risk (susceptibility) and the seriousness of the issue must happen first. You are thinking just like a clinical nurse!

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of a vulvovaginal yeast infection (candidiasis)?

options.A: Yellow-green, frothy discharge with strawberry spots
options.B: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with intense itching
options.C: Thin, gray-white discharge with a strong fishy odor
options.D: Clear, watery discharge with severe lower abdominal pain

explanation: Spot on! Yeast infections are famous for that thick, white discharge and relentless itching, without a fishy smell. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which little flap of tissue automatically covers your windpipe when you swallow, keeping food out of your lungs?

options.A: The epiglottis
options.B: The uvula
options.C: The lower esophageal sphincter
options.D: The soft palate

explanation: Think of the epiglottis as a trapdoor! When you swallow, it folds down over your larynx and trachea to block food and drinks from taking a wrong turn into your lungs.

question: When should a nurse recommend a deeper medical checkup beyond basic history-taking for menstrual pain?

options.A: When the patient is a teenager experiencing her very first periods
options.B: When mild cramping is relieved easily by simple rest and warmth
options.C: When there is a strong family history of normal menstruation
options.D: When secondary dysmenorrhoea or pelvic pathology is suspected

explanation: You nailed it! If standard relief doesn't work or pain starts later in life, we need to investigate deeper for conditions like endometriosis.

question: What is the primary goal of preventive nutrition counselling?

options.A: Reviewing individual hospital charts for acute surgical patients
options.B: Prescribing medications to cure advanced infectious diseases
options.C: Stopping health problems before they start in healthy populations
options.D: Treating severe kidney failure with emergency dialysis diets

question: Why do nurses care about finding the 'central tendency' in research data?

question: Why do nurses give adjuvant medications along with regular pain relievers?

question: Why do many breast cancer patients in Nigeria sadly arrive at the hospital with advanced stages?

question: Which factor strongly influences a client's choice regarding contraceptive use?

question: What is the primary purpose of using the topical route of administration?

question: Why is the primary survey performed in a strict ABCDE order?

question: How does constant stress on a very busy hospital ward affect a nurse's day-to-day interactions?

question: During suctioning, your patient's oxygen saturation drops rapidly and their heart rate becomes irregular. What is your very first action?

question: Why are fungal infections sometimes trickier to treat than bacterial infections?

question: A patient wakes up gasping for air two hours after falling asleep and has to sit by the window to breathe. What is this called?

question: Why do doctors and nurses prefer feeding patients through the gut (enteral nutrition) rather than through a drip (parenteral nutrition) when possible?

question: What is the right approach when counseling a PAC patient on family planning and contraception?

question: Which physical sign strongly points to dehydration in a patient with severe vomiting and diarrhea?

options.C: The free, unbound drug
options.D: The drug molecules trapped in fat cells

explanation: Only the 'free' drugs—the ones not hitching a ride on proteins like albumin—are small and active enough to slip out of blood vessels and reach target receptors.

question: How can you best support parents whose baby is in Gallows traction?

options.A: Tell them not to touch the child at all
options.B: Explain the setup and involve them in gentle, non-physical comforting
options.C: Ask them to leave the room until it's over
options.D: Teach them how to adjust the heavy weights

explanation: Parents feel helpless seeing their baby in traction. Teaching them how to talk, sing, and stroke the baby keeps that parent-child bond strong!

question: What are the three classic symptoms of a pheochromocytoma (an adrenal medulla tumor)?

options.A: Hypotension, hyperpigmentation, and fatigue
options.B: Headache, diaphoresis, and tachycardia
options.C: Weight gain, moon face, and purple striae
options.D: Muscle wasting, tremors, and cold intolerance

explanation: Think of a pheochromocytoma as an adrenaline factory gone wild! It triggers sudden pounding headaches, heavy sweating (diaphoresis), and a racing heart (tachycardia).

question: Why do many women hesitate to go back to a clinic for their next reproductive health checkup?

options.A: Nurses typically encourage too many follow-up visits
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable everywhere
options.C: They prefer managing all medical conditions independently at home
options.D: They experienced poor quality or disrespectful care previously

explanation: It's sad but true—if patients meet rude staff or lack privacy, they lose trust and stay away. Always aim to be the nurse who makes clients feel safe and welcome! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h1)

question: A 25-year-old patient comes in with weight gain, facial hair growth, and no periods for 8 months. Which condition fits best?

options.A: Hypothalamic amenorrhea
options.B: Premature ovarian insufficiency
options.C: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.D: Hyperprolactinemia

explanation: Exactly right! The classic trio of high male hormone signs, irregular cycles, and weight shifts points straight to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). You're doing brilliant clinical thinking!

question: Which of the following is a suitable health topic for discussion at a PTA meeting?

options.A: Malaria prevention and insecticide-treated nets
options.B: Commercial transport licensing procedures
options.C: How to write university entrance examinations
options.D: The stock market price of agricultural goods

explanation: Malaria prevention is a critical public health topic that directly affects school attendance and student well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why do patients who experience harmful traditional practices often keep it a secret from healthcare workers?

options.A: Because modern medical treatments cannot cure traditional injuries
options.B: They are usually unaware that their physical symptoms are abnormal
options.C: Fear of social backlash, punishment, or betraying family customs
options.D: Hospitals explicitly forbid patients from discussing cultural events

explanation: You're doing great! Survivors often stay quiet because they are afraid of what their community might say or do to their families.

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance at the primary health care level?

options.A: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.B: To collect taxes from patients seeking medical treatment
options.C: To detect unusual increases in cases early and report them
options.D: To construct new hospital buildings in rural districts

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on health patterns so health workers can spot a sudden spike before it becomes a major outbreak.

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used only at home, while quarantine is strictly used inside hospitals.
options.B: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts healthy people who were exposed.
options.C: Isolation applies to bacteria, while quarantine applies exclusively to viral infections.
options.D: Isolation requires wearing PPE, while quarantine requires taking chemoprophylaxis.

explanation: Remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick with an infection, while quarantine is for healthy people who were exposed and need to wait to see if they fall ill.

question: Why do smartphones and social media apps increase the risk of early unprotected sex?

options.A: They automatically increase hormone production in the adolescent brain
options.B: They allow teens to easily find partners and arrange secret meetings away from adult supervision
options.C: They replace comprehensive sex education with verified medical facts
options.D: They prevent teenagers from communicating with their peers

explanation: Digital technology provides private channels for teens to connect, flirt, and arrange hookups without parents or teachers knowing. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the main goal of setting short-term targets for a patient with a metabolic disorder?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any future nursing assessments
options.B: To permanently cure the underlying chronic endocrine disease
options.C: To achieve immediate stabilization of dangerous lab values
options.D: To replace the physician's medical treatment orders

explanation: Correct! Short-term goals are all about stepping back from the edge—like pulling a patient away from dangerously high or low blood sugar right now.

question: What Nigerian legislation explicitly bans the practice of Female Genital Mutilation nationwide?

options.A: The National Minimum Wage Decree
options.B: The Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.C: The Federal Highway Safety Regulation
options.D: The Environmental Sanitation Edict

explanation: Correct! The VAPP Act provides the legal backing that criminalizes harmful traditional practices like FGM across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which room in a typical home is considered the most dangerous for slip and fall injuries?

options.A: The bathroom
options.B: The kitchen
options.C: The living room
options.D: The bedroom

explanation: Wet surfaces combined with hard porcelain fixtures make the bathroom the site of many severe household falls. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the best way to ask a patient about sensitive reproductive topics?

options.A: Asking rapidly to get through the uncomfortable questions quickly
options.B: Only asking if the patient brings up the topic first
options.C: Leaving the questions blank on the form for the doctor to handle
options.D: Building trust first to encourage honest and open sharing

explanation: Well done! Patients can feel shy or worried. Building a warm, non-judgmental space helps them open up so you can give the best care.

question: A new mum just had a repair for a fourth-degree tear and is terrified of her first toilet trip. What should be in her care plan?

options.A: Providing daily enemas to clear the lower bowel completely
options.B: Instructing her to restrict all oral fluid intake until she passes stool
options.C: Applying strong pressure dressings over the anus to prevent stool passage
options.D: Administering prescribed stool softeners and encouraging high-fiber foods

explanation: Soft stools mean she won't have to strain, which keeps the delicate stitches in her anal area safe and undisturbed.

question: A nurse starts feeling emotionally numb and dreads coming to work after losing several patients. What is the best first step for this nurse?

options.A: Talk things over with colleagues or a supervisor in a support session
options.B: Hide the feelings so nobody thinks you are weak
options.C: Ignore the feelings and pick up extra night shifts
options.D: Resign from nursing immediately

explanation: Never bottle it up! Talking with supportive colleagues helps process heavy emotions and protects you against burnout.

question: What is the proper term for healthcare services given to a woman during pregnancy?

options.A: Paediatric surveillance
options.B: Postpartum recovery
options.C: Antenatal care
options.D: Gynecological screening

explanation: Antenatal care (ANC) is simply the medical supervision and support given to an expectant mother throughout her pregnancy. You've got this!

question: Where does the growing uterus usually push the stomach during pregnancy?

options.A: Downward and deep into the pelvis
options.B: Upward and to the left
options.C: Forward against the anterior abdominal wall
options.D: Directly backward against the spine

explanation: As the baby grows and takes up space below, the stomach gets nudged upward and slightly to the left. Makes sense when you picture it!

question: Which of these is a direct positive patient outcome linked to having highly motivated nurses?

options.A: Higher frequency of disciplinary hearings for junior staff
options.B: Increased total cost of medical supplies per admission
options.C: Faster turnaround times for hospital building construction
options.D: Lower rates of hospital-acquired infections and patient falls

explanation: When nurses are motivated and alert, they pay close attention to safety checks, which directly protects patients from preventable slips, falls, and infections.

question: A nurse manager says, 'We must sterilize the surgical instruments every morning at 7 AM.' What kind of activity is this?

options.A: An objective
options.B: A mission
options.C: A goal
options.D: A task

explanation: Spot on! Doing a specific duty at a set time is a daily task that keeps the clinic running smoothly.

question: In which section of the fallopian tube does fertilization usually occur?

options.A: Ampulla
options.B: Fimbriae
options.C: Isthmus
options.D: Cervix

explanation: The ampulla is the wide middle section where sperm and egg typically meet and fertilize. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is a key focus when nursing an expectant mother who has chronic kidney disease?

options.A: Administering prophylactic dialysis starting in the first trimester
options.B: Strict blood pressure monitoring and medication adherence support
options.C: Restricting fluid intake entirely to prevent maternal edema
options.D: Encouraging a high-protein diet to replace lost urinary nutrients

explanation: Keeping blood pressure in check takes the pressure off the kidneys and keeps the placenta happy and well-supplied with blood.

question: What is the right step after cleaning a patient's fingertip with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Wait for the alcohol to dry completely on the skin
options.B: Blow on the finger to speed up the drying process
options.C: Wipe the wet alcohol off with a sterile gauze pad
options.D: Prick the wet finger immediately to save time

explanation: If the alcohol is still wet, it mixes with the blood drop and dilutes it, giving you a false reading. A few seconds of patience guarantees an accurate result!

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to handle used needles?

options.A: Putting sharps containers right next to where you work
options.B: Avoiding bending needles before throwing them away
options.C: Dropping the whole syringe and needle into a safety box
options.D: Recapping needles using both hands right after use

explanation: Using both hands to recap is a top way nurses accidentally stick themselves. Always avoid it!

question: What is a vector in the context of disease transmission?

options.A: A living organism, usually an insect, that carries a pathogen to a host
options.B: An open skin lesion that allows bacteria to enter the bloodstream
options.C: A drug resistant bacterial strain found in hospital wards
options.D: A contaminated hospital instrument used on multiple patients

explanation: Vectors are living carriers like mosquitoes, ticks, or fleas that transfer infectious agents from one animal or human to another. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a main source of laboratory-based surveillance data?

options.A: Confirmation of specific germs and drug resistance patterns
options.B: Commercial market prices for staple foods
options.C: Records of primary school student attendance
options.D: Daily weather forecasts and rainfall measurements

explanation: The lab tells us the exact culprit making people sick and whether standard drugs can fight it off or if the germ is resistant.

question: A student wants to study post-operative pain across fifty hospitals nationwide in just two weeks with zero funding. What is the major flaw here?

options.A: Patients do not experience pain after surgery
options.B: The topic is completely unrelated to nursing care
options.C: Hospital staff never want to improve pain management
options.D: The study lacks practical feasibility due to time and budget limits

explanation: We would all love to save the world in two weeks for free, but it's simply not realistic! Always make sure your study matches your actual time and pockets.

question: Which compress is best for a patient who twisted their ankle just ten minutes ago?

options.A: Alternating hot and steaming compress
options.B: Room-temperature dry wrap
options.C: Cold compress
options.D: Warm compress

explanation: For fresh injuries (acute injuries), cold therapy is your best friend to keep swelling and pain down.

question: Why do we place a waterproof sheet on an operation (surgical) bed?

options.A: To protect the mattress from bodily fluids, blood, and drainage
options.B: To anchor the top blankets securely to the bed frame
options.C: To keep the patient cool during high fever episodes
options.D: To provide extra cushioning for bony prominences

explanation: Spot on! Patients coming from theatre might bleed or vomit, so a waterproof sheet keeps the mattress safe and clean.

question: What is the primary immunological benefit of early colostrum feeding for a newborn?

options.A: Lowering infant red blood cell destruction rates
options.B: Supplying complete proteins for muscle growth
options.C: Providing high concentrations of secretory IgA antibodies
options.D: Preventing the development of physiological jaundice

explanation: Colostrum is packed with antibodies that coat the baby's digestive tract, protecting them from harmful bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h6)

question: Why must work inside the TSSU always flow in one direction?

options.A: To reduce the electricity consumption of heavy sterilizing machines
options.B: To prevent clean and sterile items from mixing with dirty ones
options.C: To make it easier for nursing students to clean the floors
options.D: To speed up the physical movement of heavy instrument trays

explanation: Exactly! Keeping a one-way workflow ensures items only move forward from dirty to clean, protecting patients from cross-contamination.

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the emergency ABCDE assessment framework?

options.A: Breathing
options.B: Blood pressure
options.C: Bleeding
options.D: Bone fracture

explanation: In emergency triage, B stands for breathing to ensure the victim is receiving adequate oxygen exchange. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h5)

question: When is a doctor most likely to prescribe a drug like ranolazine?

options.A: When the patient has an extremely slow resting heart rate
options.B: When standard drugs fail to control chronic stable angina
options.C: When treating an acute emergency heart attack in the ER
options.D: When high blood pressure is the primary diagnosis to treat

explanation: Think of ranolazine as a trusty backup plan—it's usually brought in when the usual first-line medications aren't quite getting the job done on their own.

question: When a mother stops breastfeeding and her milk-producing parts shrink back down (involution), what cellular process is mainly responsible?

options.A: Fibrotic scarring of the alveoli
options.B: Hypertrophy of adipose tissue
options.C: Calcification of the milk ducts
options.D: Apoptosis of secretory cells

explanation: Apoptosis just means 'programmed cell death.' When milk isn't needed anymore, the extra milk-making cells quietly tidy up and shut down.

question: What is it called when a patient with kidney failure has a dangerous buildup of potassium in their blood?

options.A: Hypercalcemia
options.B: Hyperkalemia
options.C: Hypoglycemia
options.D: Hyponatremia

explanation: Break the word down: 'hyper' means high, 'kalium' is the Latin root for potassium, and 'emia' means in the blood. When kidneys fail, they can't clear out potassium, leading to hyperkalemia.

question: What happens during a paradoxical response to a sedative?

options.A: The patient falls into an irreversible multi-day coma
options.B: The patient becomes extremely agitated instead of calm
options.C: The drug has zero physical or emotional effect at all
options.D: The patient develops hives and facial swelling instantly

explanation: Paradoxical means 'opposite'! Instead of calming down from a sedative, the patient goes the other way and gets super restless. You're doing great!

question: What happens when a community actively participates in planning its own local health programs?

options.A: The programs are more likely to succeed and last long-term
options.B: Western medicine is completely rejected by the villagers
options.C: The government stops funding public health services entirely
options.D: Nurses no longer need to work in rural health centers

explanation: When people help build a program, they take ownership of it, making it much more sustainable over time. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: An injured survivor of an assault arrives at your facility. What is your very first clinical priority?

options.A: Conducting a detailed psychological interview
options.B: Filing mandatory police incident reports
options.C: Collecting forensic swabs and clothing fibers
options.D: Stabilizing life-threatening physical injuries

explanation: Saving a life and stabilizing the patient always comes first before collecting evidence or paperwork.

question: When giving perineal care, in which direction should you wash to prevent spreading germs?

options.A: From the rectum toward the urethral meatus
options.B: From side to side across the pubic bone
options.C: In a circular motion starting from the outer thighs inward
options.D: From the urethral meatus toward the rectum

explanation: Always think 'front to back'! Wiping from the urinary opening toward the back keeps nasty bowel bacteria away from the urinary tract, preventing painful UTIs.

question: Why is data encryption so important for health wearable devices?

options.A: To increase the physical durability of the wristband strap
options.B: To protect sensitive patient health records from unauthorized interception
options.C: To ensure the step counter measures distance more accurately
options.D: To make the device battery last much longer during daily use

explanation: Encryption scrambles personal health details so hackers can't read or steal confidential patient information.

question: A nurse notices that a patient's skin is very dry and lacks normal turgor. Which physiological issue does this most likely suggest?

options.A: Dehydration and fluid volume deficit
options.B: Excessive vitamin D production
options.C: Normal localized blood pooling
options.D: High levels of subcutaneous fat

explanation: Poor skin turgor and dryness are classic clinical signs of fluid loss and dehydration. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h8)

question: What causes that unpleasant smell in some gas?

options.A: Sulfur compounds produced by specific gut bacteria
options.B: The breakdown of proteins by liver enzymes
options.C: High levels of pure oxygen from swallowed air
options.D: Undigested stomach acid reaching the rectum

explanation: Certain helpful (and smelly!) bacteria release tiny amounts of sulfur when they break down food. Totally normal body process!
